Here is a broad review from ChatGPT on **#25, #30, #32, #38, and #40–#44:** 

# Review sweep completed

I posted **nine review summaries and 13 new inline resolution threads**. One previously posted unresolved CI thread also remains open on #41. The reviews use `COMMENT` rather than `REQUEST_CHANGES` because the authenticated GitHub account owns the PRs; the findings themselves are explicitly marked as required resolutions.

For the scientific rollout PRs, I used the thesis’s distinction between factual replay, actor-visible state, privileged selected-depth evidence, and the planned task-sufficient dynamic scene state as an alignment reference. 

## Reviews and required resolutions

| PR                                                 | Review                                                                                       | Main required resolutions                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| -------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **#25 — Apple-Silicon Mojo backend**               | [Review](https:/<redacted:machine-path> | Remove the unrelated Matt Pocock skill/OMX scaffold payload from the backend PR. Avoid making the personal PyTorch3D fork the unconditional dependency for Linux CPU/CUDA installations, or define an explicit maintenance and upstream-parity contract. The PR currently changes 199 files despite describing the product-code delta as surgical.                                                                                                        |
| **#30 — Scaffold and auditable thesis links**      | [Review](https:/<redacted:machine-path> | Do not reintroduce the obsolete `python-docstrings` owner removed by #42. Salvage only still-unique thesis-link and upstream-Graphify commits into focused PRs; do not attempt to merge the conflicted 134-commit, 392-file historical branch wholesale.                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| **#32 — Rollout generation, audit, and inspector** | [Review](https:/<redacted:machine-path> | Choose one authoritative implementation between #32 and #38 before resolving conflicts. Deepen the approximately 3.7k-line string-keyed inspection surface behind one immutable inspection snapshot with a few typed domain views. Split the repository-wide `.configs/` relocation from the scientific rollout feature.                                                                                                                                  |
| **#38 — Scientific stored-rollout evidence**       | [Review](https:/<redacted:machine-path> | Do not merge this alongside #32. Publish a salvage matrix and close one of the overlapping branches. Collapse the separate generation audit, scientific-audit, and inspection vocabularies into a single typed artifact flow: generation emits, scientific audit validates/aggregates, inspector renders. The current PR is conflicted and spans 144 files.                                                                                               |
| **#40 — Shared worktree environment**              | [Review](https:/<redacted:machine-path> | Make `--check` validate that `mamba` and the named environment actually exist, or remove the second environment owner and invoke the already-linked venv directly. The current check can report readiness while the only advertised command wrapper fails immediately.                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| **#41 — Direct ARIA skills and Aria Grill**        | [Review](https:/<redacted:machine-path> | Do not land tracked transcript evidence before the validator introduced only in #44; either move the first artifact downstream, bring the validator into #41, or merge the stack atomically. Do not promote deprecated `design-an-interface` as a first-class route; use the maintained `codebase-design` design-it-twice workflow or establish an explicitly ARIA-owned replacement. The pre-existing hosted-CI coverage thread also remains unresolved. |
| **#42 — Python documentation ratchet**             | [Review](https:/<redacted:machine-path> | Either enforce the ratchet through required CI in this layer or narrow the claim to introducing the tool; enforcement currently arrives only in #43. Make the stale-owner test use NUL-delimited byte-safe `git ls-files` parsing, matching the hostile-filename guarantees of the production ratchet.                                                                                                                                                    |
| **#43 — Causal CI tiers**                          | [Review](https:/<redacted:machine-path> | Ensure package/API changes cannot bypass the API-documentation contract. Remove duplicate execution of `qh-ci` and the Python ratchet across scientific and package jobs; create a shared prerequisite or make tier ownership disjoint.                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| **#44 — Commit transcript provenance**             | [Review](https:/<redacted:machine-path> | Capture an explicit commit-relevant message slice rather than every eligible user/assistant message in the entire repository session. The present behavior can publish unrelated discussion from long-lived threads; regex redaction does not make unrelated content causally relevant or appropriate to retain.                                                                                                                                          |

## Highest-priority cross-PR decisions

1. **Resolve #32 versus #38 first.** They are competing, conflicted implementations of substantially the same rollout-generation, audit, topology, and inspection area. Merging both would recreate duplicate ownership.

2. **Treat #41–#44 as an atomic policy stack or revise each layer’s claims.** #41–#43 already add transcript artifacts and trailers, while the executable validator lands only in #44. A prefix merge currently leaves repository policy and enforcement temporarily inconsistent.

3. **Close or replace #30 rather than rebasing it wholesale.** Its useful thesis/Graphify work should be salvaged separately; its scaffold and Python-documentation ownership has been superseded by #41–#44.

4. **Split #25 before resolving its merge conflicts.** The backend change and the agent-skill vendoring are independent review and rollback units.

5. **Prefer deep interfaces over large dictionary vocabularies.** The most important remaining codebase-architecture opportunity is the rollout inspection path: one admitted store should produce one typed, immutable inspection snapshot, rather than several thousand lines of loosely coordinated dictionary schemas shared between audits, panels, tests, and Rerun adapters.

Reviewed PRs #40–#44 at their current heads. All are `REQUEST CHANGES`; architect status is `BLOCK` for each. No P0 findings.

Required blockers:

- #40: readiness check does not validate its advertised `mamba` runner.
- #41: transcript evidence precedes enforcement; Aria Grill routes to deprecated `design-an-interface`.
- #42: ratchet is not enforced in this layer; stale-owner test is not byte-safe; transcript policy is still unenforced.
- #43: package API changes bypass API-doc validation; overlapping tiers duplicate expensive checks; transcript policy is still unenforced.
- #44: “commit-scoped” provenance captures whole sessions, not a commit-relevant message slice.

I published two new inline P1 review threads for the previously unthreaded #42 and #43 prefix-policy defects: [#42 review](https:/<redacted:machine-path> and [#43 review](https:/<redacted:machine-path> Existing unresolved threads already cover the other findings, so I did not duplicate them.

I’m switching to the isolated #44 publish worktree. I’ll preserve the existing provenance mechanism, narrow capture to an explicit commit-relevant slice, and prove older same-repository discussion cannot enter the artifact before committing locally.

The smallest coherent contract is a required UTC timestamp boundary: `<redacted:high-entropy-token>` marks when commit-relevant discussion begins, capture excludes every earlier message even in the same repository/session, and the canonical boundary participates in both snapshot identity and payload validation.

The new regression passes: an earlier same-repository message is excluded, only messages at/after the explicit boundary remain, and tampering with that boundary fails snapshot-identity validation even after recomputing the outer payload hash. I’m now exercising the full hook transaction and static checks.

All 52 provenance tests, 24 CI-impact tests, hook end-to-end, Ruff, strict mypy, and memory validation are green. I’m amending only #44 now with a freshly scoped artifact from this task’s session start; the lower-stack artifacts remain untouched and will disappear when the parent rebuilds #44 on the artifact-free #41–#43 chain.

The first amend failed closed before mutating the index: this native subagent session contains both child and root `session_meta` records, so exact-session parsing resolves to the root thread identity. I’m retrying against an isolated snapshot of this same session file using its final root-thread identity; the explicit timestamp still restricts capture to this #44 task only.

The retry exposed a real exact-session bug in the existing extractor: it selects a file by the first `session_meta`, then overwrites that identity when a native child session embeds its root-thread metadata. I’m repairing that narrow invariant—session identity is established once by the first metadata record—so native subagent provenance remains exact rather than relying on a rewritten temporary snapshot.

PR #44 is repaired locally at `<redacted:high-entropy-token>`; worktree is clean and unpushed.

Implemented:

- Required explicit `<redacted:high-entropy-token>`.
- Excluded earlier same-repository/session messages.
- Hash-bound and validated canonical `capture_scope` metadata.
- Added scope-tampering and native-child-session regressions.
- Regenerated #44’s own valid artifact/trailer.

Verification:

- Provenance tests: 53/53
- CI-impact tests: 24/24
- Hook end-to-end: passed
- Ruff, strict mypy, agent-memory validation: passed
- `validate-range HEAD^ HEAD`: passed
